# ChartKit JSON spec

> @chartkitdev/core v0.5.0
> Schema: https://chartkit.dev/schema/v1.json
> `import { render } from "@chartkitdev/core/all"`
> `import { repair, validate } from "@chartkitdev/core/validate"`

This file describes the JSON spec. React component props are in the last section. They are not keys in the spec.

## Rules

- `version` is `"1"`. `a11y.alt` is one sentence and is required.
- `data` is a plain array of row objects. It is not `{ "values": [...] }`. Sparkline, mini-area, and spike may use a plain number array. Large data may use `{ "columns": { "field": [] } }`.
- The chart type goes in `type`. `mark` is an options object (`curve`, `sampling`, `layout`), not a string.
- Gauge, kpi, and progress-ring put the number in `metric`: `{ "value", "min", "max", "delta", "label" }`. Those keys are not top-level. A `data` object of the same fields moves into `metric`.
- Donut uses `encoding.x` (slice label) and `encoding.y` (slice value). Not `theta`, `angle`, or `label`.
- `encoding.*.axis` is the string `"y"` or `"y2"`. Titles go in `axes.y.title` or `axes.y2.title`.
- Field types are `quantitative`, `temporal`, `ordinal`, or `nominal`. Not `categorical`.
- A heatmap with `encoding.x`, `encoding.y`, and `encoding.color` is a grid. A calendar heatmap is a date `x` plus `color`, or `mark.layout: "calendar"`. The measure is `encoding.color`, not `encoding.value`. `grid-heatmap` and `calendar-heatmap` are `heatmap` plus `mark.layout`.
- Combo is one spec. `encoding.y` is `[{ "field", "mark": "bar" }, { "field", "mark": "line", "axis": "y2" }]`. Not `layer`, `layers`, `marks`, or `encoding.bar` / `encoding.line`. A list of fields goes on `encoding.y`, not on `field`. On a combo, `bar`, `line`, and `area` go in `mark`, not in `type`.
- A bar splits long data with `encoding.series`, or with `encoding.color` when that value is a field. `mark.stack` is `"stack"` or `"percent"`. `scale.type` `"log"` is a log axis. A temporal `x` is a time axis. `format` on an axis or channel is applied to the ticks. Rule, band, and text `annotations` are drawn. Tooltip, zoom, pan, brush, animation, `legend.interactive`, and `a11y.keyboard` / `a11y.dataTable` are valid; when one is turned on, `validate` warns CK3011 because the SVG does not draw it yet. The default theme is `auto` (transparent, follows `prefers-color-scheme`, overridable with `--ck-*` or `--chart-N`). `theme: "midnight"` is the dark card.

## Repair loop

Recommended agent loop:

1. `const result = validate(spec)`.
2. When `result.ok` is false, call `repair(spec)`. It applies the safe JSON Patch on each error (`fix`) and returns `{ spec, ok, errors, applied }`. The input spec is not mutated.
3. Render `repair(spec).spec` when `ok` is true. When errors remain, follow those hints. A missing or unknown `type` is reported first, with a patch, and without every other chart type's required fields.

`repair` only applies patches `validate` already produced. It does not invent data.

## line

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "line",
  "data": [
    { "quarter": "Q1", "units": 40 },
    { "quarter": "Q2", "units": 55 },
    { "quarter": "Q3", "units": 48 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "quarter", "y": "units" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Units peaked in Q2." }
}
```

## bar

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "bar",
  "data": [
    { "lane": "A", "stops": 12 },
    { "lane": "B", "stops": 7 },
    { "lane": "C", "stops": 15 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "lane", "y": "stops" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Lane C has the most stops." }
}
```

## donut

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "donut",
  "data": [
    { "wood": "Oak", "boards": 8 },
    { "wood": "Pine", "boards": 5 },
    { "wood": "Maple", "boards": 3 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "wood", "y": "boards" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Oak is the largest share of boards." }
}
```

## stacked-area

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "stacked-area",
  "data": [
    { "year": "2022", "rail": 20, "road": 30 },
    { "year": "2023", "rail": 24, "road": 28 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "year", "y": ["rail", "road"] },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Road stayed larger than rail." }
}
```

## scatter

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "scatter",
  "data": [
    { "temp": 16, "yieldKg": 3 },
    { "temp": 22, "yieldKg": 5 },
    { "temp": 27, "yieldKg": 4 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "temp", "y": "yieldKg" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Yield is highest at 22 degrees." }
}
```

## combo

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "combo",
  "data": [
    { "week": "W1", "orders": 30, "rate": 0.4 },
    { "week": "W2", "orders": 36, "rate": 0.55 }
  ],
  "encoding": {
    "x": "week",
    "y": [
      { "field": "orders", "mark": "bar" },
      { "field": "rate", "mark": "line", "axis": "y2" }
    ]
  },
  "axes": { "y2": { "title": "Fill rate" } },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Orders and the fill rate both rose." }
}
```

## heatmap

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "heatmap",
  "data": [
    { "bin": "A", "band": "Low", "level": 1 },
    { "bin": "B", "band": "Low", "level": 4 },
    { "bin": "A", "band": "High", "level": 2 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "bin", "y": "band", "color": "level" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Bin B in the low band is the darkest cell." }
}
```

## gauge

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "gauge",
  "metric": { "label": "Capacity", "value": 64, "min": 0, "max": 100 },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Capacity is 64 out of 100." }
}
```

## kpi

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "kpi",
  "metric": { "label": "Tickets", "value": 18, "delta": -0.05 },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Open tickets are 18, slightly down." }
}
```

## sparkline

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "sparkline",
  "data": [4, 6, 5, 9, 8],
  "a11y": { "alt": "The sparkline ends higher than it starts." }
}
```

## mini-area

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "mini-area",
  "data": [2, 3, 3, 6, 5],
  "a11y": { "alt": "The mini area rises, then eases." }
}
```

## progress-ring

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "progress-ring",
  "metric": { "label": "Done", "value": 3, "min": 0, "max": 8 },
  "a11y": { "alt": "3 of 8 items are done." }
}
```

## spike

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "spike",
  "data": [
    { "slot": "t1", "hits": 0 },
    { "slot": "t2", "hits": 6 },
    { "slot": "t3", "hits": 1 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "slot", "y": "hits" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "Hits spike at t2." }
}
```

## candlestick

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "type": "candlestick",
  "data": [
    { "day": "D1", "open": 5, "high": 7, "low": 4, "close": 6 },
    { "day": "D2", "open": 6, "high": 6, "low": 3, "close": 4 }
  ],
  "encoding": { "x": "day", "open": "open", "high": "high", "low": "low", "close": "close" },
  "a11y": { "alt": "The second session closed below its open." }
}
```

## React components (not the JSON spec)

`@chartkitdev/react` also exports components. Their props (`dataKey`, `leftAxis`, `value` on `GaugeChart`) are not spec keys. To render a spec, use `<Chart spec={...} />`.

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| `LineChart`, `BarChart`, `DonutChart`, `StackedArea`, `ScatterChart`, `ComboChart` | Dashboard components. Prefer a spec for agents. |
| `Heatmap`, `GaugeChart`, `KpiCard`, `Sparkline`, `MiniArea`, `ProgressRing`, `SpikeChart`, `CandlestickChart` | Same. Metric components take `value` as a prop; the spec uses `metric`. |
| `Chart` | Renders a JSON spec. |

## Framework adapters

The same spec renders in React, Vue, Svelte, and a plain element. Each wrapper asks `@chartkitdev/core` for an SVG string. There are no extra spec keys.

- React: `import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/react"` and `<Chart spec={spec} />`.
- Vue 3: `import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/vue"` and `<Chart :spec="spec" />`. `renderToString` from `@chartkitdev/vue/ssr` includes the SVG.
- Svelte 5, and Svelte 4: `import { Chart } from "@chartkitdev/svelte"` and `<Chart {spec} />`. The component uses `export let`. SvelteKit SSR includes the SVG.
- Vanilla: `import { mount, renderToString } from "@chartkitdev/vanilla"`. `mount(element, spec)` returns `{ update(spec), destroy() }`. `renderToString(spec)` is the SVG string core returns.

`spec` in each of those is the line example above (`quarter` / `units`), or any other spec in this file. Pass `render` from `createRenderer([...])` to ship one chart type.
